newsitem.title: JORDAN: King Hussein back in Jordan after surgery in U.S..
newsitem.headline: King Hussein back in Jordan after surgery in U.S..

text.p: King Hussein returned to Jordan on Friday after surgery in the United States on an enlarged prostate gland, the official Petra news agency said.
"I am well now. The operation was not easy, but thank God the result was positive and good," the agency quoted him as saying on arrival at Amman airport.
The king, 61, said he needed a few days' rest before he went back to work, Petra said. Officials said earlier on Friday he had postponed a planned April 22-25 visit to Denmark.

The king underwent surgery last Saturday at the Mayo Clinic in Minnesota on a benign enlargment of the prostate gland. He was advised to stay in hospital for a week to be followed by two weeks of recuperation.
King Hussein began his U.S. trip three weeks ago with a visit to the Mayo clinic, where he has returned annually for routine checkups since surgery in 1992 for cancer.
Doctors said they had not detected any evidence of a recurrence of the cancer, but recommended the prostate operation, saying it was normal for a man of the king's age.
During his visit the monarch also held talks in Washington with U.S. President Bill Clinton on growing Arab-Israel hostility threatening a four-year-old Palestinian self-rule accord.
The king was also visited at his bedside last Sunday by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu who was on his way to talks with U.S. officials.
